notes.31: 28% of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B, chosen by 41% of candidates. For many candidates this question therefore rested on the truth, or otherwise, of statement 3. Statement 3 is true, the key word in the question being unpaired. A carbon atom has two p electrons, therefore it has two unpaired p electrons. A Cl+ ion has four p electrons, therefore it has two paired and two unpaired p electrons.
notes.40: 25% of candidates chose the correct answer, D. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C, chosen by 56% of candidates. It is possible that many candidates saw C in the question and then chose statements 2 and 3 because these statements each had a compound with four carbon atoms per molecule, either butanedioic acid or methylpropanedioic acid. However, if either of these compounds is reacted with calcium metal it can produce a salt with empirical formula CaC H O , but not CaC H O . However ethanoic 4 4 4 4 6 4 acid, CH CO H, reacts with calcium metal to produce calcium ethanoate, Ca(CH CO ) , which does have empirical formula CaC H O .
